title: Growth recording table
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Soils and aquatic plants (Flow and One Planet, Our World)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 30 (Growth recording table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 30: Recording plant growth. To understand how to measure and record plant growth accurately

questions.q: A seedling reaches the 5 on the ruler, starting from 0 at the soil. How tall is it?
questions.model: Zero sits on the soil. The top leaf lines up with 5. So the seedling is 5 cm tall.

questions.q: Which looks healthier: yellow and floppy, or green and upright?
Why do we write 'cm' after the number?
questions.a: So everyone knows the unit we measured in

questions.q: Measure three seedlings in each pot and record the middle height for each soil.
questions.a: A table with three heights in cm; loam usually tallest
questions.model: Teacher measures one seedling from the loam pot on camera: 'zero at the soil... 4 cm'.

questions.q: Describe how the plants in each pot look. Use the word 'healthy'.
questions.a: For example: 'The loam cress is green and healthy; the sand cress is short and some leaves are dry.'

questions.q: Was your prediction right? Write one sentence.
questions.a: Pupils' own answer linked to their results

questions.q: Big question: how can you prove which cress is taller?
questions.a: Measure each from the soil to the top with a ruler, in cm.
